AESF 5050.title: Fracture Behavior of Polymers
AESF 5050.description: Introduction to both fundamental and practical knowledge on the microstructure, physical and mechanical behaviors, particularly the fracture behavior and toughening mechanisms, of polymers and composites. Discussions and critiques on related research activities in the literature. Case studies to help students prepare for the industry.
cilos: Explain the microstructure-property relationships of polymers and select proper polymeric materials for specific engineering applications.
Characterize polymer fracture and evaluate fracture toughness of polymers using rigorous fracture mechanics methods under various conditions.
Explain the fundamental fractography of polymers and carry out basic failure analysis using microscopes and thermal analysis equipment.

AESF 5210.title: Fluid Dynamics
AESF 5210.description: Basic concepts of fluid flows, derivation of governing equations, viscous flow, potential flow, boundary layer, flow instability, transition to turbulence, turbulent boundary layer.
cilos: Apply fluid mechanics knowledge to certain practical problems.
Explain some fluid mechanics related phenomena in daily life.
Analyze practical fluid mechanics problems.

AESF 5310.title: Advanced Aerodynamics
AESF 5310.description: Circulation, Kutta-Joukowski theorem, thin airfoil theory, lifting line theory, wingtip vortices, induced drag, elliptical wings, boundary layers, normal and oblique shocks, bow shocks, Prandtl-Meyer expansion fans, linearized potential flow theory, Prandtl-Glauert transformation, wave drag, transonic flow, swept wings, critical Mach number, supercritical airfoils.
cilos: Apply the basic tools of incompressible inviscid aerodynamic analysis to estimate lift and drag for an airfoil.
Explain and quantify the effects of viscosity on airfoil performance.
Explain the differences in aerodynamic performance between an infinite-span (2D) airfoil and a finite-span (3D) wing.
Account for the effects of compressibility in aerodynamics situations.

AESF 5320.title: Advanced Aircraft Structures
AESF 5320.description: Aircraft structural design, wing structural details, elasticity, maneuver and gust loading, fatigue analysis, vibration theory, static and dynamic aeroelasticity, energy and matrix methods.
cilos: Apply the fundamental equations of elasticity to aircraft loading situations.
Use various deformation theories and fatigue analyses to obtain analytical solutions for situations in aircraft structural deformation.
Specify the materials used in aircraft structures and identify their failure modes.
Apply the basic principles of stressed-skin aircraft construction.

AESF 5330.title: Advanced Aircraft Design
AESF 5330.description: Flight mission requirements, aircraft size and layout, airfoil/wing geometry, aerodynamics, engine selection, airframe−engine integration, fuselage design, electrical and hydraulic systems, landing gear arrangement, flight stability and control, structures and materials, avionics and navigation systems, human factors, safety, manufacturing processes, and cost analysis.
cilos: Apply the formal design and development process for aeronautical vehicles.
Optimize aircraft/engine design and airframe-engine integration.
Create feasible designs integrating a variety of aircraft systems and sub-systems.
Test and verify the feasibility of aircraft designs.

AESF 5350.title: Advanced Aircraft Propulsion
AESF 5350.description: Propulsion cycle analysis, with emphasis on gas turbines, basic component performance and function, engine installation effects, aero-thermodynamics of steady isentropic compressible flow, shock waves, diffusers and nozzles, centrifugal compressors, axial flow compressors, combustion chambers, thermoacoustics, fuels and control, turbines, thrust augmentation.
cilos: Make design choices between aircraft propulsion systems based on perfonnance considerations.
Calculate energy release, e.g. adiabatic flame temperatures, and equilibrium composition of gases at known temperatures and pressures.
Analyze the thermodynamic performance of engine cycles and compute relevant performance parameters.
Size jet engines using preliminary design calculations.

AESF 5350.title: Aircraft Propulsion
AESF 5350.description: Propulsion cycle analysis, with emphasis on gas turbines, basic component performance and function, engine installation effects, aero-thermodynamics of steady isentropic compressible flow, shock waves, diffusers and nozzles, centrifugal compressors, axial flow compressors, combustion chambers, thermoacoustics, fuels and control, turbines, thrust augmentation.
cilos: Make design choices between aircraft propulsion systems based on perfonnance considerations.
Calculate energy release, e.g. adiabatic flame temperatures, and equilibrium composition of gases at known temperatures and pressures.
Analyze the thermodynamic performance of engine cycles and compute relevant performance parameters.
Size jet engines using preliminary design calculations.

AESF 5370.title: Composites and Nanocomposites
AESF 5370.description: This course is designed to provide fundamental understanding of fiber-reinforced composites (FRPs) and emerging nanocomposites technologies. The topics include constituent materials, microstructure-property relationships, fabrication and processing techniques, fundamental mechanics of stress transfer, lamination theory and failure mechanisms and fracture of FRPs in the first part. The topics in the second part include synthesis of nanoscale reinforcements, fabrication and processing techniques of nanocomposites; dispersion and functionalization of nanoreinforcements; interfacial adhesion; mechanical and functional properties of nanocomposites, and their design and applications.
cilos: Distinguish different fabrication and processing methods for FRPs and nanocomposites.

Explain the mechanical and functional properties of these composites based on the microstructures/properties of the fillers and the matrix material, as well as the way how these constituents are combined to produce composites.
Identify potential applications of FRPs and nanocomposites utilizing these properties.
Identify the mechanics of stress transfer through the filler/matrix interface and interphase, lamination theory and failure mechanisms behind the fracture of FRPs and nanocomposites.

AESF 5380.title: Computational Fluid Dynamics
AESF 5380.description: Fundamental knowledge of computational fluid dynamics, specific applications of CFD to industrial and environmental flows, learn how to write a complex two-dimensional solver and some engineering applications.
cilos: Apply the basic theory of Computational Fluid Dynamics, including discretisation, accuracy and stability.
Assess the impact of fluid mechanics problems commonly encountered in industrial and environmental settings.
Construct and apply computational models, determine critical control parameters and relate them to desired outcomes.
Use a state of the art commercial computational fluid dynamics package for numerical simulations of fluid mechanics problems.

AESF 5630.title: Avionics Technology
AESF 5630.description: Avionics are today at the very heart of the aircraft, controlling and monitoring a safe and efficient mission. Upon completion of this course, students will be able to present an accurate overview of what is an avionics platform, its systems, functions and operations. The course covers system fundamentals, current instruments and future development.
cilos: Identify how to derive the performance of various avionics systems.
Assess the requirements for individual avionics subsystems and provide guidance for future development.
Define the architecture of modern avionics and demonstrate conceptual understanding of its integration design.

AESF 5710.title: Hong Kong Airworthiness
AESF 5710.description: The civil aviation industry is one of the safest modes of transportation, yet complex and highly regulated. Almost every part of the industry is regulated. From the design, manufacturing and operation of an aircraft, people operating and maintaining the aircraft to organizations handling, operating and maintaining the aircraft, all are regulated by various rules and regulations. This course introduces the concept of airworthiness and examines the framework of both international and Hong Kong aviation regulations governing the aviation industry, allowing the students to understand the whole journey of the life of an aircraft.
cilos: Identify and explain the difference between Initial and Continuing Airworthiness.
Identify the applicable airworthiness regulations that an aircraft needs to comply with during its operating life and the conditions for safe operation.
Identify how operations and organizations in the aviation industry are regulated.

AESF 5720.title: Aerospace Materials and Applications
AESF 5720.description: Advances in aerospace systems such as aircraft, spacecraft, and launch vehicles are strongly dependent on advances in materials and processing technologies. This course aims to introduce aerospace materials and their applications in different aerospace systems. It equips students regarding the selection of the materials and their applications in various systems. It attempts to cover the entire field of aerospace materials in a condensed fashion with emphasis on aerospace structures and propulsion systems applications. At the end of this course, students are expected to achieve a comprehensive idea about how to select the best available material in every case in the field of aerospace engineering.
cilos: Recognize the visualization of the complexity of structural components and materials of the aerospace vehicles and understand their functions.
Apply the commonly used aerospace materials: metals and alloys, polymers, composites, and ceramics for different applications.

Identify a variety of functional requirements with constraints (manufacturability, geometric limits, environmental aspects, etc.) to arrive at the “optimum” choice of structural concept and materials selection for a given weight and/or cost.
Identify the capability to solve the real-world problems with engineering mindset.

AESF 5730.title: Airline Marketing
AESF 5730.description: In the airline business, marketing and airline/aircraft engineering work closely together, fulfilling the company vision, mission and strategy. This course covers the fundamental concepts of marketing, focusing on the airline business and the interrelationship with engineering in making the business a success.
cilos: Identify the fundamental concepts of marketing, focusing on the airline business.
Identify the interrelationship between airline marketing and airline/aircraft engineering.
Apply acquired knowledge to analyze airline marketing  projects/campaigns, figuring out the role of engineering.

AESF 5740.title: Building Airport Operational Resilience
AESF 5740.description: One of the most affected industries in our inter-connected and inter-dependent world is civil aviation, which at one point collapsed to just 5% of its former self because of the effects from a pandemic. One lesson learned in the aviation industry is the need for all industry stakeholders to build up operational resilience. Strengthened operational resilience enables all stakeholders to meet risks and threats that are inter-connected and that can come from anywhere around the globe. This course will explore what is operational resilience, why it is important, and how to achieve it.
cilos: Identify aviation risks and threats in the 21st century aviation risk landscape.
Identify and explain the crossroads concept of 21st century airport management.
Identify the importance of operational resilience.
Examine building operational resilience and need for integration amongst all stakeholders within the airport community.

AESF 5750.title: Strategic Procurement Management in Aviation Industry
AESF 5750.description: In a rapidly evolving global market, aviation companies must enhance their capabilities or risk losing market share. This course explores how strategic procurement management can be a critical tool for survival and success in the aviation industry. With a focus on the impacts of outsourcing and offshoring, students will learn to manage procurement processes and mitigate risks effectively, understanding how these strategies influence the profitability and success of airlines and maintenance organizations in today’s competitive business environment.
cilos: Acquire a comprehensive understanding of the strategic procurement management process and identify its potential value creation.
Distinguish between strategic and tactical activities, recognizing their unique impacts and applications.
Utilize a diverse set of tools and techniques to thoroughly analyze internal and external environments.
Develop an appropriate strategy selection framework that analyze internal and external environments and create value for their organization.
Acquire a thorough grounding of negotiation planning for sourcing plan development.
Design effective value-for-money evaluation mechanisms to select the best offers in an objective and transparent manner.
Establish and manage efficient processes to ensure the performance of strategic sourcing contracts.
Design and implement a supplier management process focused on compliance with the statement of work and ensuring performance standards are met.

AESF 5760.title: Flight Data Application in Maintenance, Safety, Efficiency and Flight Tracking
AESF 5760.description: Basic concept of aircraft avionic system in data communication and recording and making use of actual flight data from aircraft avionic system to manage aircraft maintenance program, operational safety, flight efficiency, and carry out flight tracking procedure in an airline.
cilos: Comprehend different avionics systems involved in aircraft data acquisition.
Recognize how transmitted data can enhance maintenance practices.
Understand the requirements for flight tracking.
Recognize the operational limitations for aircraft tracking and the  emergency procedures when an aircraft is missing.
Identify various industry best practices in achieving flight efficiency through the use of flight data and analysis.
Identify current constraints in aviation infrastructure and technical challenges related to improving fuel efficiency and reducing emissions.
Analyze flight data for safety purposes and accident investigations.
Identify industry best practices in Safety Management Systems and Flight Data Analysis Programs.

AESF 5930.title: Finite Element Methods
AESF 5930.description: Finite element formulation; variational principles for structural and continuum mechanics; numerical interpolation and integration; plane stress and plane strain analysis; plate bending and three dimensional solids; solution of large systems of algebraic equations.
cilos: Derive finite element formulations for structural mechanical problems and heat conduction.
Implement finite element methods for simple 1-D problems such as truss analysis and 1-D heat conduction either by hand calculation or by programming.
Numerically evaluate stresses, strains and deformation of a structural component due to axial load, torsion, and bending, acting individually or in combination.
Numerically calculate temperature profile and heat flux in 1-D and 2-D heat conduction problems.
Numerically evaluate stresses, strains and deformation of a structure under either plane-stress or plane-strain conditions.
Derive finite element formulations for time-dependent and/or non-linear problems.
Perform structural analysis and heat transfer modeling using commercial software package, and conduct engineering design in a team work environment.

AESF 6910-6920.title: Special Topics
AESF 6910-6920.description: Selected topics in aeronautical engineering of current interest in emerging areas and not covered by existing courses. May be repeated for credit if different topics are covered.
cilos: Identify the updated development in the emerging area and apply the knowledge accordingly.

AESF 6950.title: Aeronautical Independent Project
AESF 6950.description: An independent research project on Aeronautical Engineering carried out under the supervision of a faculty member.
cilos: Address the existing problems in Aeronautical/Aerospace Engineering through literature search and technical communication.
Apply acquired knowledge to analyze and investigate existing problems on Aeronautical/Aerospace Engineering.
Design solutions to improve the existing techniques and conduct experiments/numerical simulations in the Aeronautical/Aerospace Engineering area.
